content: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) complications become more common and severe as kidney function deteriorates, especially in individuals with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Laboratory evaluations should be performed at intervals based on the stage of CKD: every 6 to 12 months for patients with stage G3 CKD, every 3 to 5 months for those with stage G4 CKD, and every 1 to 3 months for individuals with stage G5 CKD. The frequency of these assessments should be adjusted depending on the severity of symptoms and any changes in treatment.
